svg.aria-label: compaction: keep the last per key
svg.text: The changes and the current state — stack and heap at every step
9 changes → 2 entries · compaction drops 7 and changes nothing present · 7 past values lost
1 // primitive: len(xs) — element count. len(CHANGELOG) = 9 · keys = 2
2 // primitive: CHANGELOG — one entry per change, in order. Each says what a key BECAME.
3 // CHANGELOG = a=5 a=8 b=7 a=10 a=16 b=8 b=17 b=21 a=24
4 // primitive: TABLE — a key to its current value. One entry per key, no history.
6 // primitive: keyOf(e) / valOf(e) — the two fields of an entry.
9 // primitive: keysOf(t) — the keys a table holds, in order.
11 // primitive: UNANSWERABLE — the question cannot be answered from what is kept.
12 // primitive: entry(k, v) — one changelog entry.
16 // "You have a sequence of changes, each saying what a key became. Produce the current
17 // value of every key. Then: produce the changes back from the table. Then: the log is
18 // too long to keep — what may you discard, and what do you lose?"
20 // function: fold(log) — the changes into the state. Later entries overwrite earlier ones,
21 // so the order of the log is the whole content of the answer.
31 // function: emit(t) — the state back out as changes. One entry per key, and that is
42 // function: compact(log) — keep only the LAST entry per key. Everything dropped was
43 // superseded, so the state the log folds to does not change.
44 // compact(CHANGELOG) = a=24 b=21 — 7 of 9 entries dropped
53 // function: valueAfter(log, k, n) — what key k was after its n-th change. Answerable
54 // from the full log and from nothing else.
68 // function: main() — fold, emit, compact, then ask about the past.
73 val same = fold(small) // a:24 b:21 — identical
Step 5/0 — compaction: keep the last per key
a=24 b=21 — **7 of 9 entries dropped**. Every one of them had been superseded by a later entry for the same key, so nothing that the table depends on was removed,
which the next frame checks rather than assumes.
